host.dbus: DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS removed for every app measured

metrics.label: Cold start to first paint
metrics.plain: Time from double-click to the page being visible
metrics.method: exec -> first frame containing the page's own marker colour, polled from the framebuffer at ~4 ms; fresh profile and fresh X server per run. Not screenshot-mode minus a baseline: that path carries a fixed 900 ms settle.

metrics.label: Memory, one tab open
metrics.plain: Memory the app uses sitting idle with one tab
metrics.method: Sum of Rss over every process in the app's pid tree (/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup), 60 s after the tab loaded. Pss is reported too: Rss double counts pages shared between processes.

metrics.label: Extra memory per parked space
metrics.plain: Memory added by each agent space kept in the background
metrics.method: (RSS with 4 spaces - RSS with 1 space) / 3, same page in every space, 60 s after load. The three parked spaces are WasHidden(true); the app reports 'parked' in its log, which the harness counts.

metrics.label: CPU while idle
metrics.plain: Share of one processor core wasted while nothing is happening
metrics.method: Delta of utime+stime over the whole process tree across a 60 s window, 4 spaces (3 parked, the visible one included), divided by the window: percent of one core. Kernel jiffies, so ±0.02 %.

metrics.label: Snapshot, median
metrics.plain: Time for an agent to read the page it is looking at
metrics.method: 30 snapshots per run x 3 runs on the long list (2412 nodes), through 'ego-browser nodejs' with ROOK_BACKEND=host (bridge -> control socket -> CEF), viewport scope (the default). Each run's own p50, then median and spread across runs.

metrics.label: Snapshot, p95
metrics.plain: Time for an agent to read a heavy dashboard, slow case
metrics.method: Same samples as the p50 row; p95 of each run on the heavy dashboard (3797 nodes, 5794 snapshot lines), median and spread across runs.

metrics.label: Installed size
metrics.plain: Disk space the package takes after installing
metrics.method: dpkg's Installed-Size field of the .deb (KiB -> MB), i.e. what dpkg reports for the installed tree. The compressed .deb and the AppImage are listed for context.

baselines.label: Chrome, headless, one tab
baselines.plain: Plain Chrome with one page open, for comparison
baselines.method: google-chrome --headless=new, one page loaded, RSS over the chrome pid tree after a 20 s window.

baselines.label: Chrome, headless, cold start
baselines.plain: Time for plain Chrome to produce a rendered frame
baselines.method: exec -> PNG written by --screenshot, warm profile. Headless Chrome has no window, so there is no framebuffer to poll; this is its own equivalent measurement, not the same instrument as the Rook number.

contributors.title: The CEF runtime, counted once per process (587 MiB of the 940 MiB)
contributors.detail: RSS sums every process in the tree, and each of the 10 processes maps the same 330 MB libcef.so. The gap between summed RSS (940 MiB) and summed Pss (353 MiB) is that double count. It is not memory the app can give back, but a budget written as "total RSS" pays for it once per process, so the number of processes is itself a cost.

contributors.title: One renderer process per space (130 MiB per extra parked space)
contributors.detail: 4 spaces cost 1335 MiB against 940 MiB for 1: 130 MiB per space. Parking a space (WasHidden(true)) throttles its timers but does not drop its renderer: all four awake is 1312 MiB, i.e. 23 MiB more. The per-space renderer is the cost; parking is only worth -6 % of it.

contributors.title: Snapshot cost scales with the page, not with the viewport (26 µs per element)
contributors.detail: p50 goes from 5 ms at 21 elements to 66 ms at 2412 elements and 141 ms at 3797 elements, i.e. about 26 µs per node. Filtering to the viewport does not avoid that work: the same call without the filter (`scope: "full_page"`) costs 71 ms instead of 66 ms on the long list and 154 ms instead of 141 ms on the dashboard, because Accessibility.getFullAXTree reads the whole document before anything is filtered out. The host socket is not the cost: the same call against the bridge's own headless Chrome, with no app process in between, takes 74 ms against 66 ms here.
